OFF-AGENDA, FOR EXPLORERS:  full timeline  ·  places  ·  what shaped my taste
DRAG  pan     SCROLL  zoom     HOLD  take control

This isn't a slide deck or a video. It's an engine I built
to present it: canvas, recorder, voice-synced cursor.
An infinite canvas, in real DOM.

Pan, zoom, edit. Every word here is real text,
and one JSON file is the whole CMS.
A tour that's data, not video.

I drive the camera while I talk. It saves keyframes
on an audio clock and replays at any screen size.

Hold anywhere and he hands you the wheel.
Click him and he picks up where he left off.

$ cat how-this-works.txt

· playback is a pure function of time
· zoom lerps in log space, feels linear
· tours contain-fit to any screen
· hold to take over, click a_r to resume
· frames skip React, commit at rest
· the CMS is one JSON file

EXHIBIT A
simula_r.com, the board you're on

Research before solutions. Design school, real engineering,
and 1999 → now across London, Dubai, Europe and California.

· Parsons, design school
· First paid gig: business cards
· Internships in design, video, print
· Still sweats the 1px stuff

· Early startups, logo to prod deploy
· {{SV startup}}: London · Dubai · Europe
· ComfyUI, San Francisco

· First computer in 1999, first opinions too
· Graphics, games, tools, product

· Home: California, near family + mountains

Every good jam sets principles before solutions.
These are mine, for design engineering in the AI era.

AI made average free.
Taste is the moat.
Generation is cheap. Knowing what's good isn't.
Mocks thrown over a wall lose half their intent.
Feel it, find what's wrong, fix it in the real material.
The prototype is the product now, so craft it.

BS

velocity theater
mocks nobody builds
"AI will replace taste"
meetings about meetings

NOT BS

shipping
reading the source
sweating 1px
small teams, big swings

Anyone can put "design engineer" on a resume.
Here's the proof, strongest first.
I design and ship real product, at scale.
I know where every pixel comes from.

I write the renderer in C and push bytes into
the framebuffer myself.

Also: reverse-engineering a big design tool's C++ engine,
just to see how it stays that fast.

I make the part of games
you look at.

A web game where everything you see is 3D art
I made: models, levels, lighting, the mood.

A strange 3D walking simulator that lives
inside a Winamp skin. All art, no apologies.
Every jam ends in a decision. I made this one easy.

Post the role again. Read more portfolios
that are just PDFs.

One hire, both halves: the designer and the
engineer, same PR, no handoff.

Work that's hard and real: a team with actual
initiative, building something that should exist.
That's where the interesting problems are, and
where craft actually matters.

California, close to family, close to

in the woods.
